info.title: Practical info
info.subtitle: What to know before you go.
info.disclaimer: General information: always check official sources before departure.

language.title: Languages
language.text: French is the official language. Fon, Yoruba, Dendi, Bariba and other languages are spoken depending on the region.

currency.title: Currency
currency.text: CFA franc (XOF), pegged to the euro at a fixed rate.

electricity.title: Electricity
electricity.text: 220 V, 50 Hz. Type C and E sockets: bring an adapter.

health.title: Health
health.text: Yellow fever vaccination is required. See a doctor before you travel.

entry.title: Entry
entry.text: Visa and documents: check with the Benin embassy or the official website.

holidays.title: Public holidays
holidays.note: Muslim holidays and days decreed by the government are not included: check the official calendar.

unesco.q: In what year were the Royal Palaces of Abomey inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List?

exile.q: Which king of Dahomey surrendered in 1894 before being exiled to Martinique?
exile.exp: Béhanzin, exiled to Martinique and then to Algeria.

jan10.q: What is January 10 dedicated to in Benin?
jan10.exp: It is the Day of Indigenous Religions, also called the Vodun festival.

gate.q: Which city is home to the Door of No Return?
gate.exp: Ouidah, at the end of the Slave Route.

capital.q: What is the official capital of Benin?
capital.exp: Porto-Novo is the official capital; Cotonou hosts the government.

bronze.q: Which technique is used to cast bronze in Beninese craftsmanship?
bronze.exp: Lost-wax casting: the object is modelled in wax, then the metal replaces the wax.

rename.q: In what year did Dahomey become Benin?

currency.q: What is the currency of Benin?
currency.exp: The CFA franc (XOF), pegged to the euro at a fixed rate.

gelede.exp: Gèlèdè pays tribute to mothers and their spiritual power.

fort.q: The São João Baptista de Ajudá fort in Ouidah was founded by Portugal in…
fort.exp: In 1721. It now houses the Ouidah History Museum.
